dedupe_keys.name: bgs mining hazard not including coal great britain

description: This BGS dataset maps the location, extent and hazard level of former and present underground mine workings in Great Britain other than coal, such as ironstone, gypsum, lead, chalk and tin. It combines bedrock geology, reviews of published and unpublished literature, abandonment and mine plans and expert knowledge, grouped into seven mining themes, and rates each area on an A (mining not known) to E (extensive underground mining known) scale. Version 8 (2021, DOI 10.5285/9a558ef2-0081-4e86-917f-ae60b9df40a2) adds newly identified areas, draws on the BritPits database and for the first time includes zones of influence around evaporite, oil shale and building stone workings. Coverage is Great Britain at 1:50 000 scale; related products listed on data.gov.uk are version 7, a 1 km hexagon grid generalisation, the original 2010 A to E layer and a re-attributed layer rating susceptibility to infiltration for sustainable drainage. Access: the BGS product page lists it as a premium product priced at £0.35 per km2, subject to number of users, licence fee and data preparation fee, supplied as GIS polygon data (ESRI, MapInfo, other formats on request); copyright is vested in NERC and reuse needs BGS permission. Caveats: coverage is not complete, as areas without evidence of underground working are not included, and coal workings are left to the Mining Remediation Authority. For simulation it gives a national subsidence and collapse hazard layer for ground stability checks on roads, rail, pipelines and buildings above old workings. Related catalogue records include BGS BritPits and the Mining Remediation Authority Development High Risk Area.
